chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the disbursement of the Dirhams coated over. So he said: 'When it was such that the silver overwhelmed upon it, so there is no problem'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on spending Dirhams coated with silver?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on dirhams coated with other metals, establishing that if silver remains the dominant metal (ghalib), the dirham retains its permissibility for use. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the intrinsic value and legal status of currency are determined by the predominant material, ensuring clarity in commercial transactions and charity disbursement. It underscores the importance of material composition in determining the validity of monetary instruments in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the disbursement of the Dirhams coated over. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was such that the silver ovewhelmed upon it, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Umar Yazid who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about spending dirhams with impurities.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If the amount of silver is overwhelming in it, it is not unlawful. 5 ”
